title: Executed and imagined grasp forces recorded with stereo-EEG (Murphy et al., 2016): 4 participants, power and pinch force-matching
description: Stereo-EEG recordings from four adults with drug-resistant epilepsy performing force-matching tasks with a power grasp and a lateral pinch. Two participants also completed blocks in which they only imagined producing the force. Each block contained trials at three force targets (20, 30 and 40% of maximum voluntary contraction). The data comprise 46 blocks (about 2.11 h) sampled at 2000 Hz, with an analog dynamometer channel and force-target events. They support study of how subsurface cortical modulations discriminate executed and imagined grasp forces.
methods_description: Neuroport amplifier recordings at 2000 Hz with an analog dynamometer force channel. Participants matched force targets shown for 5 s, alternating with 5 s rest, in blocks of 5 trials per target. Blackrock NSx int16 samples were converted unchanged to BrainVision format, and target periods from the Simulink log were written to events.tsv. Dates were partially de-identified.
